- category: This is an "Automatic level gauge" — under R85, automatic level gauges for measuring level of liquid in storage tanks. Category could be "Automatic level gauge" or "Level gauge". Let me use "Automatic level gauge".
- type_designations: ["NMS530", "NRF 560"] — NMS530 is the level gauge, NRF 560 is the remote indicator (optional component).
- module_designation: null (not applicable — not a modular instrument per R60 style). The schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Not mentioned, so omit or null. I'll omit? Rules say "Don't fabricate. If a field is not present in the markdown, omit it." So omit module_designation. Hmm, but for consistency, I could set null. Better omit.
- description: "Automatic level gauge for measuring the level of liquid in storage tanks, make Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd., model NMS530, optionally equipped with a remote indicator, make Endress+Hauser Japan Co., Ltd., model NRF 560."

Components: remote indicator NRF 560, optional. Role: "remote indicator", type_designations ["NRF 560"], alternatives: null (it's optional, not OR alternative). The level gauge itself NMS530 could be a component too — role "level gauge" (main instrument). I think include components: main instrument NMS530 and optional remote indicator NRF 560. Alternatives for the remote indicator: it's "optionally equipped" — not exactly OR alternative in the sense of alternatives. I'd leave alternatives null.

Characteristics type_level: From the table:
- Accuracy class: 2 — this goes to recommendation.accuracy_classes = [2], and possibly characteristics? I think accuracy class belongs in recommendation. The table lists "Accuracy class: 2", "Minimum product level: 0 m", "Maximum product level: 28 m".

The other columns contain text descriptions:
- Liquid pressure/temperature: "-40 … +200 °C; the gauge was tested at environmental temperatures of –25 °C, +55 °C and in the range from 20 °C … +24 °C." — this is about liquid temperature range -40 to +200 °C. Extract as characteristic liquid_temperature_range: {min: -40, max: 200}, unit °C. The tested environmental temperatures is a note — could go into description or a footnote? Not a footnote. Could add characteristic environmental_test_temperatures as list? The rules say lists of values of Emax → model matrix. But this is testing info; probably keep as string value or omit. I could add a characteristic "liquid_temperature_range" and maybe "tested_environmental_temperatures": value string "-25, 55, 20...24 °C". Hmm. Let me keep it simpler: 
  - liquid_temperature_range: {min: -40, max: 200} °C
- Vapour pressure: "Vacuum … 25 bar gauge" → vapour_pressure_range: {min: null, max: 25}, unit "bar (gauge)"? Unit symbol "bar gauge" — hmm. I'd say value {min: null, max: 25}, unit_symbol "bar(g)". Better: unit_symbol "bar gauge"? Canonical: "bar". Maybe include as string "Vacuum … 25 bar gauge" value? Rules want structured. I'll do value {min: null, max: 25}, unit_symbol "bar", and maybe note gauge. Actually "25 bar gauge" means gauge pressure. unit_symbol "bar(g)" is a reasonable raw symbol. I'll use "bar(g)". Hmm, risky. Alternatively value: "Vacuum ... 25 bar gauge" as string. I think structured with unit "bar(g)" is fine. Or use min null, max 25, unit "bar gauge". Let me use unit_symbol: "bar(g)". Hmm, I'll go with "bar(g)"? Actually simplest to keep parseable: unit_symbol "bar" and add characteristic note? There's no notes field for type-level values except footnote_markers. I'll just include the text description in matrix_tables? The table itself could be a matrix_table! 

Actually the table on page 1 is a table with columns: Accuracy class, Minimum product level, Maximum product level, Min/max values for liquid pressure/temperature/properties, Min/max vapour pressure/temp/properties, Liquid characteristics, Liquid density extreme values. This is more of a characteristics table than a matrix. I could preserve it in matrix_tables with description and also extract structured characteristics.

Approach:
- type_level characteristics:
  - accuracy_class: 2 (dimensionless) — but also in recommendation. Including in both is fine? The schema example includes accuracy_classes in recommendation. I'll put accuracy class only in recommendation to avoid duplication. Hmm, but the table lists it as a characteristic. I'll include it in type_level too? To be safe, include in recommendation only. Actually many extractions include accuracy_class as a characteristic. I'll include it as type_level "accuracy_class": {"value": 2, "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null}. That's fine.
  - minimum_product_level: {value: 0, unit_symbol: "m"}
  - maximum_product_level: {value: 28, unit_symbol: "m"}
  - liquid_temperature_range: {min: -40, max: 200} °C
  - environmental_test_temperatures: string? The tested temps: -25 °C, +55 °C, and 20…24 °C. Could be "tested_environmental_temperatures": value "-25 °C, +55 °C, 20 °C … +24 °C"? That's messy. Maybe omit and put in matrix_tables description. I'll keep the whole table as a matrix_table row preserving raw text, and extract clean numeric characteristics separately.

  - rows: one row with raw text values.
  - description: explaining it's from page 1.
